apiDocs.title: Public API
apiDocs.description: A few of our endpoints answer without a session on purpose — the ones EuroScope, the ATIS client and the live map call. They are documented here so you can build against them too.
apiDocs.englishNotice: The reference is written in English. Parameter names, headers and response fields are English on the wire, and a translated copy of a wire format is one more thing to keep in step.

auth.detail: There is nothing to apply for. Most endpoints below are open; the log upload takes an CAN ID and network password in the request body. Everything else under `/api` needs the website's own session cookie and is not a public interface.

envelope.detail: JSON answers carry a `status` and a `timestamp` next to the payload, which usually sits under `data`. The ATIS text generator is the exception: it returns plain text, because EuroScope has no JSON parser.

errors.detail: The HTTP status is the truth. An error body carries `error` — sometimes a sentence for a human, sometimes a short key for you to translate. Each endpoint says which.

rateLimits.detail: Every endpoint is counted in a fixed window, usually per IP. Over the limit is a **429** with `Retry-After` in seconds; wait it out rather than retrying straight away. The numbers on this page are read from the running configuration, so they are the limits actually enforced.

cors.detail: Marked per endpoint. Where it says any origin, `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` is sent and a browser can call it directly.

versioning.detail: `/api/v1` is the only version. Fields get added; nothing documented here is renamed or removed without a note in the Discord and QQ group first.

oauth.detail: An application that needs to act for a member uses OAuth 2.1 authorization code + PKCE: send the member to `/oauth/authorize`, exchange the code at `/api/oauth/token`, then call with `Authorization: Bearer`. The discovery document is at `/.well-known/openid-configuration`. Ask us through the feedback form to register an application.

auth.noneHint: No key and no cookie — the rate limit is the only gate.
auth.credentialsHint: Sent in the request body; the same credentials the desktop clients connect with.
auth.oauthHint: Send an access token obtained through unified sign-in in the `Authorization: Bearer` header.
auth.oauthClientHint: The client_id / client_secret issued when the app was registered. Public clients send no secret and prove themselves with PKCE.
auth.browserHint: A browser page — the member has to be signed in here in person.

notPublic.title: What is not here
notPublic.description: There are other routes under /api, but they are not a public interface. They are listed so that not finding one reads as a decision rather than an oversight.

help.title: Questions, or something you need opened?
help.description: Send a note through the report form — it reaches the maintainer directly.

dev.tagline: Register an application here and CAN members can sign in to it with their own account.

home.title: Put CAN accounts into your application
home.description: Cerulean Aviation Network is a standard OAuth 2.1 / OpenID Connect identity provider. Members sign in to your application with their own CAN account, and what you receive is a token — never their password. Register applications, manage redirect URIs and rotate secrets here.

pkce.title: PKCE is mandatory
pkce.detail: S256 for every client, confidential ones included — the authorization code travels through the browser's address bar, and a client secret protects nothing there.

redirect.title: Redirect URIs match exactly
redirect.detail: No wildcards, no prefix matching. The one exception is the RFC 8252 loopback address, where only the port is ignored, for desktop clients.

revoke.title: Tokens revoke instantly
revoke.detail: Access tokens are opaque and checked against the database on every use. One press in a member's "authorized applications" list and the next request fails.

errors.missing_state: The sign-in request expired. Try again.
errors.state_mismatch: This sign-in did not come back from where it started, so it was stopped. Try again.
errors.exchange_failed: The token exchange failed. Try again shortly.
errors.access_denied: You pressed deny on the consent screen.

apps.title: My applications
apps.description: Applications registered here let CAN members sign in with their own account. Redirect URIs are matched in full and exactly — think before you change one, because it decides where the authorization code is delivered.
apps.empty: No applications yet. Register one and members can sign in to it with their CAN account.
apps.networkError: The network is unreachable. Try again shortly.

secret.title: This is the client_secret, and it is shown once
secret.detail: Only its hash is stored, so nobody can recover it after this box closes. Lose it and you have to rotate.

form.name: Application name
form.nameHint: This is the name members see on the consent screen. It must not be mistakable for an official network application.
form.redirectUrisHint: One per line, matched in full and exactly. https only; use http://127.0.0.1 for local development (the port may vary), and a private scheme containing a dot for mobile.
form.publicClientHint: Desktop, mobile and browser-only applications — the ones that cannot keep a secret. No client_secret is issued; they prove themselves with PKCE. This cannot be changed after registration.

delete.title: Delete "{name}"?
delete.detail: Its tokens and every member's grant go with it, and none of that can be undone. Anyone currently signed in through it is locked out immediately. To confirm, type the application name:

ground.title: Ground map preview
ground.description: Draws the Ground repository's json the way the GroundMap plugin draws it — same LOD, same colours, same stroking order. Edit one airport, drop the file in, and see it without merging first and opening EuroScope. Files are parsed in your own browser and never uploaded.
ground.local: Parsed in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.
ground.canvasLabel: Ground map canvas: drag to pan, scroll to zoom

empty.title: Drop Ground's files here
empty.detail: Per-airport sources are run through merge.py locally before drawing; the merged artefact is drawn byte for byte as it is installed on a controller's machine. Several files at once is fine.

source.what: One airport, the file you hand-edit

ground.what: The merged artefact the plugin actually reads

sct.what: Optional: runway thresholds. Without it runways are approximated from OSM

stands.what: Optional: stand numbers, where OSM has none

style.what: Optional: colours and line widths; the built-in copy is used otherwise

view.title: View
view.airportHint: Picking one airport is the ASR's Airport key: only that field is drawn. "All" is what an ACC screen does — whatever is in view, with LOD deciding the rest.

layers.title: Layers
layers.hint: These are the ASR's GroundMap_<id> switches. Dimmed rows are hidden by LOD at this view width — the plugin would not draw them at this zoom either.

notes.runwaysFromOsm: Runways are approximated from the ends of the OSM centreline. The rectangles that ship to controllers come from the sector file's thresholds — drop <FIR>.sct in as well and the two match exactly.
notes.standNamesMissing: OSM has no stand numbers for this field. The merge takes them from GRpluginStands.txt; drop that file in to see them.

openid.title: Confirm identity
openid.detail: The member's CAN ID. Every sign-in needs it.

profile.title: Basic profile
profile.detail: Name, CAN ID, controller rating, registration date.

email.title: Email address
email.detail: The address and whether it is verified.

divisions.title: Division membership
divisions.detail: Which divisions they belong to and their position endorsements.

offline_access.title: Offline access
offline_access.detail: Keeps working after the member closes the browser, until they revoke it. Do not ask for it unless you are sure.
